docs.title: Institutional Commodity & Derivatives Trade Journal
docs.text:
Welcome to the comprehensive technical documentation for the Trade Journal platform.

This platform is an institutional-grade trading journal, position risk tracker, and market intelligence suite engineered specifically for commodity and futures market practitioners, proprietary trading desks, and derivative quantitative analysts.

docs.title: Why Trade Journal?
docs.text:
Retail trading journals are almost universally designed for single-asset spot or stock trading. They assume simple "buy at X, sell at Y" models. In contrast, institutional commodity trading involves:

  1. Complex Multi-Leg Structures: Calendar spreads (e.g., \(CL\) June vs. July), butterflies (\(1MF\)), double-flies, and inter-product spreads (e.g., WTI Crude vs. Brent Crude).
  2. Contract Multipliers & Point Values: Scaling price movements across disparate units (barrels, bushels, metric tonnes, index points) and multi-currency tick valuations.
  3. Exchange Fee Schedules & Rebates: Accurate modeling of pre-rebate exchange fees versus net post-rebate execution fees.
  4. Supply & Demand Fundamentals: Ingesting CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT) positioning data alongside physical agricultural fundamentals (such as Malaysian Palm Oil Board statistics).

docs.title: Core Capabilities at a Glance
docs.text: Module Core Purpose Key Features Executive Dashboard Real-time performance & risk overview Cumulative Net PnL curve, Win Rate, Win/Loss ratio, Privacy Mode toggle. Multi-Leg Execution Strategy creation & execution Outrights, Spreads, Butterflies, Double-Flies, Inter-Product Spreads. Position Auditing Event-sourced lifecycle changes Immutable log of Open, Add, Reduce, Close actions with volume weighting. COT Positioning CFTC positioning intelligence Automated API sync for 1,300+ markets, Commercial vs. Speculator breakdowns. Palm Oil Fundamentals BMD FCPO physical market tracking Forward curves, MPOB monthly S&D balance sheets, surveyor export monitors. docs.title: Planning & Calendar
docs.text:
Successful trading requires planning setups well in advance, especially in commodities where seasonal patterns repeat year after year.

The Calendar & Planned Trades modules (/calendar/ and /planned/) allow traders to pre-formulate trade hypotheses and track execution fidelity.

docs.title: 1. Trade Planning (PlannedTrade)
docs.text: Traders can submit trade plans before entry with detailed reasoning and chart screenshots:

docs.title: Recurrence Options:
docs.text:
• Once: Single setup planned for a specific date.
  • Monthly: Recurring monthly spread roll or rebalancing thesis.
  • Yearly: Seasonal commodity setup recurring annually (e.g., February Grain Planting Intentions).
  • Specific Months: Trades targeted for specific seasonal windows (e.g., March and September contract delivery roll dates).

docs.title: 2. Interactive Calendar View (/calendar/)
docs.text: The calendar combines both Planned Setups and Realized Trade Executions on an interactive grid: - Execution Markers: Displays completed trades color-coded by performance (Green for gains, Red for losses). - Planned Alerts: Highlights active seasonal setup reminders scheduled for the current month. - Monthly Navigation: Easily cycle backward and forward across historical trading months.

docs.title: CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT)
docs.text: The Commitments of Traders (COT) module (/cot/) provides weekly positioning analytics released by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

docs.title: 1. Overview of the COT Report
docs.text:
Every Friday at 3:30 PM Eastern Time, the CFTC publishes breakdown reports reflecting trader positioning as of the preceding Tuesday. These reports illuminate: - Smart Money / Commercial Hedgers: Producers, merchants, and processors actively hedging physical inventory. - Large Speculators / Managed Money: Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs), hedge funds, and quantitative trend-followers. - Small Speculators / Non-Reportable: Retail traders and smaller market participants.

Analyzing extreme net positioning helps identify market exhaustion points, crowded trades, and high-probability reversal setups.

docs.title: 2. Supported Market Categories
docs.text:
The Trade Journal's automated market discovery engine caches over 1,300+ markets across all major exchanges:

  • Agriculture: Corn (CBOT), Soybeans (CBOT), Soybean Meal, Soybean Oil, Wheat (CBOT & KCBT), Rough Rice, Oats, Live Cattle (CME), Feeder Cattle (CME), Lean Hogs (CME), Coffee C (ICE), Sugar No. 11 (ICE), Cocoa (ICE), Cotton No. 2 (ICE).
  • Energy: WTI Crude Oil (NYMEX), Brent Crude (ICE), Natural Gas (NYMEX), Heating Oil, RBOB Gasoline.
  • Metals: Gold (COMEX), Silver (COMEX), Copper (COMEX), Platinum (NYMEX), Palladium (NYMEX).
  • Financials & FX: Euro FX, British Pound, Japanese Yen, 10Y US Treasury Notes, S&P 500 E-mini, Nasdaq 100 E-mini.

docs.title: 4. How to Sync Markets
docs.text: To ensure all market codes are up to date: 1. Navigate to the COT Report page (/cot/). 2. Click the "Sync All Markets" button in the sidebar. 3. The platform will query the CFTC API endpoint, populate cftc_markets_cache.json, and refresh the market dropdown list.

docs.title: Executive Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard (/) is the central control tower of the Trade Journal, delivering a bird's-eye view of your account performance, open risk exposures, and recent closed trade summaries.

docs.title: 1. Key Performance Metrics (KPIs)
docs.text:
At the top of the dashboard, real-time summary cards reflect aggregate trading performance:

KPI Card Formula / Definition Significance Total Realized PnL \(\sum \text{Realized PnL from Closed / Reduced Trades}\) Net dollar performance across all completed executions. Win Rate \(\left(\frac{\text{Winning Trades}}{\text{Total Closed Trades}}\right) \times 100\) Percentage of closed trades that resulted in positive net PnL. Win / Loss Ratio \(\frac{\text{Average Dollar Win}}{\text{Average Dollar Loss}}\) Profit factor measuring payout asymmetry. Open Positions \(\text{Count of trades where Status} \in [\text{'Open'}, \text{'PartiallyReduced'}]\) Live active exposures currently requiring monitoring. Fees & Commissions \(\sum \text{Post-Rebate Transaction Costs}\) Total execution costs deducted across all trades.

docs.title: 2. Cumulative Net Equity Curve
docs.text:
The interactive Equity Curve chart is generated dynamically via Chart.js:

  • Time-Series Tracking: Every PositionAdjustment event (Reduce or Close) that generates realized PnL adds a point to the time axis.
  • Transaction Cost Netting: The curve tracks Net PnL, automatically subtracting each contract's transaction fee (TC_PostRebate) scaled by leg ratios: $\(\text{Adjustment Net PnL} = \text{Gross Realized PnL} - \sum_{\text{legs}} \left( \text{TC\_PostRebate} \times |\text{Size}| \times |\text{Ratio}| \right)\)$
  • Interactive Tooltips: Hover over data points to inspect date, trade title, and cumulative balance.

docs.title: 3. Privacy Mode Toggle 👁️
docs.text:
For traders who present their setups, record educational content, or stream their screens, the Trade Journal includes a built-in Privacy Mode:

  • One-Click Activation: Click the eye icon (#privacyToggle) in the top navigation bar.
  • Instant CSS Masking: Applies a Gaussian blur (filter: blur(6px)) and disables text selection on all .sensitive-value elements.
  • Persistence: Remembers your privacy preference across page navigations using local storage.

docs.title: 4. Open Positions & Closed Summaries Tables
docs.text:
• Open Positions Table: Displays current open size, volume-weighted entry price, unrealized PnL estimate, and quick action buttons to adjust or close.
  • Closed Trades Log: Displays completion dates, gross realized PnL, target PnL, and net payout after exchange fee deduction.

docs.title: Palm Oil (FCPO) Fundamentals
docs.text: The Palm Oil Dashboard (/palm-oil/) is a specialized fundamental analysis hub tailored to traders participating in Bursa Malaysia Derivatives (BMD) Crude Palm Oil (FCPO) futures.

docs.title: 1. Why Palm Oil Fundamentals Matter
docs.text: Crude Palm Oil is the most widely consumed edible vegetable oil in the world. Its price dynamics are governed by a tight interplay between: - Biological production seasonality in Malaysia and Indonesia. - Physical import demands from major consuming nations (India, China, the EU). - Cross-commodity spreads against CBOT Soybean Oil (BO) and Dalian Palm Olein (P).

docs.title: 2. Integrated Data Pillars
docs.text: The dashboard aggregates three distinct fundamental streams:

docs.title: A. Forward Price Curve & Open Interest (PalmOilPriceAndOI)
docs.text:
• Visualizes daily settlement prices across forward contract tenors (Month 1 through Month 12).
  • Displays Open Interest (OI) concentration across contracts to highlight liquid benchmark months (typically the third contract month).

docs.title: B. MPOB Monthly Balance Sheet (MPOBData)
docs.text: Official monthly statistics published by the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB): - Production: Total CPO output in metric tonnes. - Imports: Raw oil inflows. - Exports: Total outflows to destination markets. - Domestic Consumption: Local industrial disappearance. - Ending Stocks: Month-end storage levels (critical indicator of market tightness).

docs.title: C. High-Frequency Surveyor Estimates (ExportSurveyorData)
docs.text: Before official monthly MPOB numbers are published, independent cargo inspection surveyors provide high-frequency export pulse data: - Surveyors: ITS (Intertek Testing Services), AmSpec Agri, and SGS. - Reporting Intervals: Day 1–10, Day 1–15, Day 1–20, Day 1–25, and Full Month.

docs.title: 3. Seeding Sample Palm Oil Data
docs.text:
To populate the dashboard with realistic multi-year historical data for testing:

python manage.py seed_palm_oil

This management command seeds: - 12 months of MPOB balance sheets. - Corresponding surveyor estimates from SGS, ITS, and AmSpec. - Daily forward price curves and contract open interest.

docs.title: Position Adjustments & Audit Trail
docs.text: Rather than storing a static contract count that is destructively overwritten, the Trade Journal implements an Event-Sourced Position Audit Log via the PositionAdjustment model.

docs.title: 1. Why Position Adjustments Matter
docs.text:
Real-world institutional trading rarely consists of opening 10 contracts and liquidating all 10 contracts in one transaction. Professional desks constantly: - Scale In: Add to winning positions as confirmations occur. - Scale Out (De-risk): Partially reduce size at first targets while trailing stops on the remainder. - Average Down / Rebalance: Adjust positions across changing price regimes.

A static database schema destroys historical fill context. The Trade Journal's audit trail preserves every action in chronological order.

docs.title: 2. The Four Adjustment Actions
docs.text: Action size_change PnL Effect Status Transition Open Positive (\(+N\)) None (Establishes position) Trade status \(\rightarrow\) Open Add Positive (\(+N\)) None (Blends entry price) Trade status \(\rightarrow\) Open Reduce Negative (\(-N\)) Locks in Realized PnL for closed lots Trade status \(\rightarrow\) PartiallyReduced Close Negative (\(-N\)) Locks in final Realized PnL Trade status \(\rightarrow\) Closed

docs.title: Volume-Weighted Average Entry Price (avg_entry_price)
docs.text:
When positions are added at varying prices, the platform calculates the volume-weighted average entry price across all Open and Add adjustments:

\[\bar{P}_{\text{entry}} = \frac{\sum_{i \in \{\text{Open}, \text{Add}\}} (|S_i| \times P_i)}{\sum_{i \in \{\text{Open}, \text{Add}\}} |S_i|}\]

Where: - \(S_i\) is the position size change of adjustment \(i\). - \(P_i\) is the fill price of adjustment \(i\).

docs.title: Realized PnL on Reductions (pnl)
docs.text:
When an existing position is partially reduced or closed, realized profit or loss is calculated using the weighted entry price and contract point value multiplier:

For Long Trades: $\(\text{Realized PnL} = (P_{\text{exit}} - \bar{P}_{\text{entry}}) \times \text{Multiplier} \times Q_{\text{reduced}}\)$

For Short Trades: $\(\text{Realized PnL} = (\bar{P}_{\text{entry}} - P_{\text{exit}}) \times \text{Multiplier} \times Q_{\text{reduced}}\)$

Where: - \(P_{\text{exit}}\) is the reduction/closure price. - \(\text{Multiplier}\) is resolved from Products.xlsx. - \(Q_{\text{reduced}}\) is the quantity of contracts closed.

docs.title: 4. State Recalculation Engine
docs.text: If an adjustment record is edited or deleted, services.recalculate_trade_state(trade_id) automatically re-simulates all historical adjustments in chronological order (timestamp ASC). It recalculates running open sizes, blend prices, and updates all downstream PnL figures.

docs.title: Multi-Leg Trade Execution
docs.text: A core strength of the Trade Journal is native support for complex multi-leg derivative strategies across commodities and futures markets.

docs.title: 1. Supported Strategy Structures
docs.text: The platform models strategies through a parent Trade object containing one or more associated TradeLeg records:

docs.title: A. Outrights (1 Leg)
docs.text: A direct directional position on a single contract month. - Example: Long 5 contracts of CL (WTI Crude Oil) Jun 2026.

docs.title: B. Calendar Spreads (2 Legs)
docs.text: Simultaneously buying and selling different expiration months of the same commodity to capitalize on forward curve slope changes (Contango / Backwardation). - Leg 1: Buy 1x CL Jun 2026 - Leg 2: Sell 1x CL Jul 2026 - Ratio Representation: [1, -1]

docs.title: C. Butterfly Spreads (3 Legs)
docs.text: A neutral spread combining an inner short strangle/straddle flanked by outer long contracts to profit from stable spread differentials with defined risk. - Leg 1: Buy 1x M1 (Month 1) - Leg 2: Sell 2x M2 (Month 2) - Leg 3: Buy 1x M3 (Month 3) - Ratio Representation: [1, -2, 1]

docs.title: D. Double-Flies (4 Legs)
docs.text: Four-legged calendar structure balancing curvature across two intermediate contract months. - Leg 1: Buy 1x M1 - Leg 2: Sell 3x M2 - Leg 3: Buy 3x M3 - Leg 4: Sell 1x M4 - Ratio Representation: [1, -3, 3, -1]

docs.title: E. Inter-Product Spreads (2+ Legs)
docs.text: Trading price differentials between two economically linked commodities (e.g., Brent vs. WTI Crude, Gas Oil vs. Heating Oil, or Soybean Crush: Soybeans vs. Soybean Meal + Oil). - Leg 1: Buy 1x CL Jun 2026 - Leg 2: Sell 1x BZ Jun 2026

docs.title: 2. Trade Execution Parameters
docs.text:
When submitting a trade via /trades/new/:

Parameter Type Purpose Trade Type Dropdown Identifies strategy classification (Outright, CalendarSpread, Butterfly, etc.). Strategy Template Selection Automatically populates leg ratios and relative month offsets from stored templates. Trade Date & Time Date / Time Captures precise entry timestamp (defaults to current time). Position Size Float Initial quantity of spread units entered. Entry Price Float Executed fill price for the net strategy spread or outright. Stop Loss & Target Float Planned risk boundaries for automatic reward-to-risk monitoring. Emotion Tag Dropdown Emotional state at entry (Fear, Aggressive, Confident, Going with the Flow). Analysis Sources Checkboxes Checkboxes tagging technical/fundamental catalysts (Seasonality, Price Action, COT Data, etc.). Screenshot File Upload Encodes chart setup as a base64 image stored directly with the trade record.

docs.title: 3. Atomic Execution Service
docs.text: Behind the scenes, the view delegates creation to services.open_trade(). This guarantees: 1. All legs and initial adjustments are written inside a single database transaction. 2. If an inter-product pair is detected (e.g., CL-BZ), it is automatically expanded into its constituent products. 3. Contract multipliers and pre/post rebate fees are looked up from Products.xlsx.

docs.title: Installation & Setup
docs.text: This guide details the complete installation and environment setup for running the Trade Journal locally or deploying it on a server.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Operating System: Windows 10/11, macOS 12+, or Ubuntu 20.04+ Linux
  • Python: Version 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12
  • Git: Installed and available in your system path
  • Disk Space: At least 500 MB (includes virtual environment and cached market data)

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the project from GitHub into your local workspace:

git clone https://github.com/nansari-0134/trade_journal.git
cd trade_journal

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Always use an isolated virtual environment to prevent dependency conflicts.

Windows (PowerShell)macOS / Linux 
# Create the virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate the environment
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Create the virtual environment
python3 -m venv venv

# Activate the environment
source venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Step 3: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
Install the pinned production dependencies:

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt

If you plan to build or serve the documentation locally, ensure MkDocs and the Material theme are installed:

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material

docs.title: Step 4: Apply Database Migrations
docs.text:
Initialize your local SQLite database:

python manage.py migrate

You should see output confirming that migrations for admin, auth, contenttypes, journal, and sessions were applied.

docs.title: Step 5: (Optional) Seed Sample Data
docs.text:
The application includes management commands to quickly seed common strategy templates and inter-product pairs:

# Seed standard strategy ratio templates (Spreads, Flies, Double-Flies)
python manage.py seed_strategies

# Seed common inter-product pairs (e.g., CL vs BZ)
python manage.py seed_interproduct_pairs

docs.title: Step 6: Launch the Development Server
docs.text:
Start the Django development server:

python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000

Note: If port 8000 is already in use by another application on your system, bind to port 8001 or another open port: 

python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8001

Open your browser and navigate to: http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (or http://127.0.0.1:8001/).

docs.title: Overview & Architecture
docs.text: Trade Journal is built with a decoupled, service-oriented architecture inside Django. Rather than placing business logic directly into HTTP request handlers (views), all operations are orchestrated through a dedicated service layer.

docs.title: Technical Stack
docs.text:
• Backend Framework: Django 5.2
  • Programming Language: Python 3.10+
  • Data Persistence: SQLite (expandable to PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL)
  • Data Analysis & Reference Parsing: Pandas & OpenPyXL
  • External API Ingestion: Requests with CFTC Socrata endpoint integration
  • Frontend Layer: Vanilla HTML5/CSS3, Bootstrap 5.3, FontAwesome 6, and Chart.js

docs.title: Directory Organization
docs.text:
trade_journal/
├── config/                  # Django project root configuration
│   ├── settings.py          # Application settings & middleware
│   ├── urls.py              # Root routing table
│   └── wsgi.py              # WSGI server entry point
├── journal/                 # Core domain application
│   ├── models.py            # Relational database models
│   ├── services.py          # Business logic & atomic financial calculations
│   ├── views.py             # View controllers and JSON endpoints
│   ├── urls.py              # Sub-application routes
│   ├── cot_service.py       # CFTC API ingestion & caching service
│   ├── utils.py             # Reference data loaders (Products.xlsx)
│   ├── management/commands/ # Data seeders & maintenance CLI commands
│   └── templates/journal/   # Jinja2 / Django dark-mode templates
├── docs/                    # MkDocs documentation source
├── Products.xlsx            # Master product reference sheet
├── cftc_markets_cache.json  # Cached metadata for 1,300+ CFTC markets
├── manage.py                # Django CLI management executable
├── requirements.txt         # Production and development dependencies
└── mkdocs.yml               # MkDocs configuration

docs.title: 1. Service Layer Pattern
docs.text:
All financial state transitions (opening positions, scaling in, reducing, and closing) reside in journal/services.py. All database mutations are wrapped inside @transaction.atomic blocks to guarantee consistency:

@transaction.atomic
def open_trade(trade_type, direction, legs, size, price, ...):
    # 1. Create master trade record
    # 2. Expand inter-product pairs if needed
    # 3. Create constituent TradeLeg instances
    # 4. Record initial 'Open' PositionAdjustment
    ...

docs.title: 2. Event Sourced Position Lifecycle
docs.text: Positions are never modified via destructively overwriting size fields. Every state change produces an immutable PositionAdjustment record. This allows: - Volume-weighted average entry price recalculation. - Historical auditability of execution dates, slippage, and prices. - Dynamic recalculation of realized PnL across sequential trade reductions.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Product Multiplier Resolution
docs.text:
Contracts trade in disparate units (e.g., Crude Oil in barrels, Corn in bushels, Palm Oil in metric tonnes). The system resolves the cash conversion multiplier on the fly:

\[\text{Multiplier} = \left(\frac{\text{PointValue}}{\text{DisplayFactor}}\right) \times \text{FXRate}\]

docs.title: Quickstart Walkthrough
docs.text: Follow this step-by-step walkthrough to record your first trade, monitor it on the dashboard, scale position size, and examine COT positioning.

docs.title: 1. Navigating the Interface
docs.text:
Once the server is running, the left sidebar provides access to every module:

  • ➕ Plus Button: Instant New Trade execution modal.
  • 📊 Dashboard: High-level KPIs, open positions, and net equity curve.
  • 🧾 Trades: Detailed trade log, realized PnL, and position adjustment inspector.
  • 📅 Calendar: Visual calendar of execution days and planned setups.
  • 🏷️ Product Fees: Contract specs, tick sizes, point values, and exchange fees.
  • 📊 COT Report: CFTC Commitments of Traders data and speculator curves.
  • 🍃 Palm Oil: Crude Palm Oil forward curve, MPOB balance sheets, and surveyor exports.
  • 🗂️ Strategies: Template ratio builder and inter-product pairs manager.

docs.title: 2. Entering Your First Trade
docs.text: Click the "+" button in the top left or navigate to /trades/new/:

docs.title: Step-by-Step Entry:
docs.text:
1. Trade Type: Choose Outright, Calendar Spread, Butterfly, or Inter-Product Spread.
  2. Strategy Template: If selecting a spread or fly, choose a preconfigured template (e.g., 1MS for front-month vs. second-month spread) to automatically set leg ratios.
  3. Product & Legs:
  4. For an outright: Select symbol (e.g., CL - Crude Oil) and contract month (e.g., Jun 2026).
  5. For a calendar spread: Select contract months for Leg 1 (Buy) and Leg 2 (Sell).
  6. Position Size & Price: Enter contract quantity and initial fill price.
  7. Psychology & Thesis: Record your entering emotion (Confident, Aggressive, Fear, etc.) and tag analysis sources (Seasonality, Price action, Fundamentals).
  8. Save: Click Submit Trade.

docs.title: 3. Scaling & Adjusting Positions
docs.text:
Positions are managed dynamically from the Trades screen (/trades/):

To adjust an open trade: 1. Locate the trade in the Open Positions section. 2. Click the Adjust button: - Add: Scale into the position by adding lots at a new price level. The platform automatically computes the new volume-weighted average entry price. - Reduce: Partially close a portion of the open contracts. Realized PnL is computed and locked in immediately for those contracts. - Close: Liquidate all remaining contracts. The trade is marked Closed, and final Net PnL is attributed to your cumulative performance curve.

docs.title: 4. Exploring Market Intelligence
docs.text:
Check CFTC positioning before entering futures positions by navigating to /cot/:

  1. Select your commodity market (e.g., Corn, WTI Crude Oil, Live Cattle, Sugar).
  2. The interactive chart will render:
  3. Total Open Interest
  4. Commercial Hedgers (Net Long vs. Net Short)
  5. Non-Commercial Speculators (Managed money positioning trends)
  6. Click Sync Markets to query the latest updates directly from the CFTC database.

docs.title: How to Add More Products
docs.text:
All product reference definitions, tick sizes, point values, currencies, exchanges, and transaction fee schedules are maintained in the master reference file:

📁 Products.xlsx (located at the root of the project directory)

You can inspect the currently loaded products and their parameters inside the platform at /products/fees/:

docs.title: 1. Structure of Products.xlsx
docs.text:
The Excel sheet contains the following columns for each contract:

Column Name Data Type Example Value Description Product String (Unique) CL Ticker or symbol code used in the system. Name String Crude Oil (WTI) Full human-readable commodity name. ProductGroup String Energy Commodity sector grouping (Energy, Agriculture, Metals, etc.). Exchange String NYMEX Primary exchange (e.g., NYMEX, CBOT, CME, ICE, BMD). Currency String USD Denominated currency (USD, MYR, EUR, GBP). TickSize Float 0.01 Minimum allowable price fluctuation. TickValue Float 10.0 Monetary cash value of one minimum tick. PointValue Float 1000.0 Value of one full point move (e.g., $1.00 move in CL = $1,000). DisplayFactor Float 1.0 Visual display scaling factor (often 1.0 or 100 for cents). FXRate Float 1.0 Currency conversion multiplier to USD. TC_PreRebate Float 2.50 Full exchange + clearing fee per contract prior to broker rebate. TC_PostRebate Float 1.20 Net effective transaction fee per contract after member rebate.

docs.title: 2. Step-by-Step: Adding a New Product
docs.text: Suppose you want to add E-mini S&P 500 Futures (ES):

docs.title: Step 1: Open Products.xlsx
docs.text: Open Products.xlsx in Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc, or any spreadsheet editor.

docs.title: Step 2: Add a New Row
docs.text:
Scroll to the bottom of the table and enter the contract specifications:

  • Product: ES
  • Name: E-mini S&P 500
  • ProductGroup: Equity Indices
  • Exchange: CME
  • Currency: USD
  • TickSize: 0.25 (Prices tick in increments of 0.25 points)
  • TickValue: 12.50 ($12.50 per 0.25 tick)
  • PointValue: 50.0 (1 index point = $50.00)
  • DisplayFactor: 1.0
  • FXRate: 1.0
  • TC_PreRebate: 1.85
  • TC_PostRebate: 1.15

docs.title: Step 3: Save the Excel File
docs.text: Save and close Products.xlsx.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify in the Web Interface
docs.text:
1. Refresh your browser at /products/fees/.
  2. Scroll to the Equity Indices section or search for ES.
  3. Confirm that the new contract appears with its tick value (\(12.50) and fee schedule (\)1.15).
graph LR
    Edit[Edit Products.xlsx] --> Save[Save File]
    Save --> Auto[Django Auto-Loads via Pandas on Next Request]
    Auto --> Available[Immediately Available in New Trade Form & Fees Page]

Pro Tip: You do not need to restart the Django server or run migrations when editing Products.xlsx. The helper function utils.get_products_data() re-reads the Excel spreadsheet dynamically.

docs.title: How to Add Strategies & Pairs
docs.text:
The platform allows you to create reusable Strategy Templates and Inter-Product Pairs to streamline entry of complex multi-leg combinations.

Manage your templates and pairs on the Strategies page (/strategies/):

docs.title: 1. Understanding Strategy Templates (StrategyTemplate)
docs.text: A Strategy Template stores the predefined ratio configuration of each leg relative to consecutive contract months.

docs.title: How Leg Ratios Map to Months:
docs.text:
• Ratio index 0: Front Month (\(M_1\))
  • Ratio index 1: Second Month (\(M_2\))
  • Ratio index 2: Third Month (\(M_3\))
  • Ratio index 3: Fourth Month (\(M_4\))

docs.title: Common Examples:
docs.text:
• 1MS (1-Month Calendar Spread): [1, -1] (Buy Front Month, Sell Next Month)
  • 2MS (2-Month Calendar Spread): [1, 0, -1] (Buy Front Month, Skip Month 2, Sell Month 3)
  • 1MF (1-Month Fly): [1, -2, 1] (Buy 1x \(M_1\), Sell 2x \(M_2\), Buy 1x \(M_3\))
  • Double Fly (DFly): [1, -3, 3, -1] (Buy 1x \(M_1\), Sell 3x \(M_2\), Buy 3x \(M_3\), Sell 1x \(M_4\))
  • G-Fly 2:1: [2, -3, 1] (Custom ratio weighting)

docs.title: 2. Adding a Strategy Template via the UI
docs.text:
1. Navigate to /strategies/.
  2. In the "Add Strategy Template" form:
  3. Name: Give your strategy a short label (e.g., 3MS, Condor 1:1:1:1).
  4. Category: Select Spread, Butterfly, DoubleFly, or Custom.
  5. Strategy Type: Select Calendar (Same Product, Different Months) or InterProduct.
  6. Leg Ratios: Enter a valid JSON list of integers or floats.
    • Example for a 3-month spread: [1, 0, 0, -1]
    • Example for an unbalanced fly: [1, -3, 2]
  7. Click "Save Strategy Template".

The new template will immediately appear in the Strategy Template dropdown on the New Trade form (/trades/new/).

docs.title: 3. Adding Inter-Product Pairs (InterProductPair)
docs.text: Inter-Product Pairs represent spreads traded between two different commodity underlyings (often across different exchanges).

docs.title: Common Commodity Pairs:
docs.text:
• CL-BZ: WTI Crude Oil vs. Brent Crude Oil
  • HO-RB: Heating Oil vs. RBOB Gasoline (Crack spread component)
  • ZW-ZC: Wheat vs. Corn (Feed grain spread)
  • FCPO-BO: Palm Oil vs. Soybean Oil (Veg-oil spread)

docs.title: How to Add a Pair via the UI:
docs.text:
1. Navigate to /strategies/.
  2. Locate the "Inter-Product Pairs" section on the right.
  3. In the form:
  4. Pair Name: e.g., CL-BZ
  5. Product 1 (Leg 1): CL
  6. Product 2 (Leg 2): BZ
  7. Click "Add Pair".

When entering a new trade, selecting CL-BZ will automatically generate both legs with their corresponding exchange parameters and tick conversions.

docs.title: 4. Seeding Templates via Python CLI
docs.text:
You can also programmatically seed default strategies using Django's management commands:

python manage.py seed_strategies
python manage.py seed_interproduct_pairs

docs.title: Fee Modeling & Multipliers
docs.text: In high-frequency commodity spread and butterfly trading, execution fees can account for a significant percentage of total gross profit. Trade Journal accounts for both Gross PnL and Net Realized PnL after broker/exchange fees.

docs.title: 1. Pre-Rebate vs. Post-Rebate Fees
docs.text:
Brokers and clearing members receive fee rebates based on monthly trading volume or exchange membership status:

  • TC_PreRebate (Pre-Rebate Transaction Cost): The standard rack-rate exchange and regulatory fee per contract charged to non-member participants.
  • TC_PostRebate (Post-Rebate Transaction Cost): The actual net cost per contract after volume rebates, exchange membership discounts, or clearing concessions are applied.

Both columns are stored in Products.xlsx:

Product | TC_PreRebate | TC_PostRebate
CL      | 2.50         | 1.25
FCPO    | 4.00         | 2.10
ES      | 1.85         | 1.15

docs.title: 2. Multi-Leg Fee Scaling
docs.text:
When trading a multi-leg strategy (e.g., Butterfly 1MF with ratio [1, -2, 1]), entering 1 unit of the strategy actually executes 4 contracts in the market:

  • Leg 1: 1 contract
  • Leg 2: 2 contracts
  • Leg 3: 1 contract

The transaction fee formula reflects this full execution weight:

\[\text{Trade Fee} = \sum_{l \in \text{legs}} \left( \text{TC\_PostRebate}_l \times |\text{Trade Size}| \times |\text{Leg Ratio}_l| \right)\]

For 10 units of a 1MF Crude Oil butterfly (\(10 \times 4 = 40\) contracts total): $\(\text{Fee} = 1.25 \times 10 \times (1 + 2 + 1) = \$50.00\)$

docs.title: 3. FX Translation to USD
docs.text: For products denominated in foreign currencies (e.g., FCPO in Malaysian Ringgit MYR, Milling Wheat EBM in Euros EUR): - FXRate in Products.xlsx establishes the conversion multiplier to base currency (USD). - Gross PnL, Net PnL, and transaction fees are converted into USD terms for consistent portfolio-wide accounting.

docs.title: Trade
docs.text: The root parent model representing a trade ticket. Holds directional stance (Long, Short), status (Open, PartiallyReduced, Closed), psychology metadata, and targets.

docs.title: TradeLeg
docs.text: Represents an individual leg inside a multi-leg trade. Contains the product symbol, contract expiration month (e.g., Jun 2026), leg direction (Buy or Sell), and ratio multiplier.

docs.title: PositionAdjustment
docs.text: The audit trail event record. Every mutation (Open, Add, Reduce, Close) creates a timestamped record storing size_change, price, and calculated pnl.

docs.title: CotReport
docs.text: Local cache of US CFTC Commitments of Traders data. Indexed by (report_date, market_code) to prevent duplication.

docs.title: PalmOilPriceAndOI, MPOBData, ExportSurveyorData
docs.text: Specialized physical commodity fundamental tables storing forward prices, open interest curves, MPOB balance sheets, and cargo surveyor export estimates.

docs.title: Multiplier & PnL Formulas
docs.text: This reference specifies the exact mathematical formulas used across the Trade Journal calculation engine in journal/services.py.

docs.title: 1. Contract Multiplier Resolution
docs.text:
Commodity contracts express price in different conventions (e.g., dollars per barrel, cents per bushel, points per index). To convert price spread differences into cash values, the service layer computes:

\[\text{Multiplier} = \left(\frac{\text{PointValue}}{\text{DisplayFactor}}\right) \times \text{FXRate}\]

If PointValue is not defined, it defaults to:

\[\text{Multiplier} = \left(\frac{\text{TickValue}}{\text{TickSize}}\right) \times \text{FXRate}\]

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
• WTI Crude (CL): \(\text{PointValue} = 1000\), \(\text{DisplayFactor} = 1.0\), \(\text{FXRate} = 1.0 \implies \mathbf{1000.0}\)
  • E-mini S&P (ES): \(\text{PointValue} = 50.0\), \(\text{DisplayFactor} = 1.0 \implies \mathbf{50.0}\)
  • Corn (ZC): \(50 \text{ bushels/contract}\) quoted in cents: \(\text{Multiplier} = \left(\frac{5000}{100}\right) = \mathbf{50.0}\)

docs.title: 2. Weighted Average Entry Price
docs.text:
When scaling into an existing trade ticket through multiple Open and Add adjustments:

\[\bar{P}_{\text{entry}} = \frac{\sum_{i \in \{\text{Open}, \text{Add}\}} (|S_i| \times P_i)}{\sum_{i \in \{\text{Open}, \text{Add}\}} |S_i|}\]

Where: - \(|S_i|\) is the absolute volume of contracts entered in adjustment \(i\). - \(P_i\) is the executed price of adjustment \(i\).

docs.title: 3. Realized PnL Calculation
docs.text:
For every Reduce or Close adjustment:

Long Trades: $\(\text{PnL} = (P_{\text{exit}} - \bar{P}_{\text{entry}}) \times \text{Multiplier} \times Q_{\text{exit}}\)$

Short Trades: $\(\text{PnL} = (\bar{P}_{\text{entry}} - P_{\text{exit}}) \times \text{Multiplier} \times Q_{\text{exit}}\)$

docs.title: 4. Net PnL (After Transaction Costs)
docs.text: \[\text{Net PnL} = \text{Realized PnL} - \sum_{l \in \text{legs}} \left( \text{TC\_PostRebate}_l \times Q_{\text{exit}} \times |\text{Ratio}_l| \right)\]
